judged_text: Salesforce (packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-95) now performs an unconditional network refresh plus credential DB write in the constructor's async flow on every service instantiation with no expiry check (previously refresh was deferred to jsforce), and it bypasses refreshOAuthTokens entirely — inconsistent with the pattern applied to 9 sibling services — so in sync mode the stored refresh_token is the 'refresh_token' placeholder and the direct fetch to login.salesforce.com fails on every operation.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the service now performs an immediate token refresh via a direct `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` and then writes updated credentials to DB (`prisma.credential.update(...)`) during service setup (right after reading `credential.key`). There is no expiry/need check before doing this refresh, so it will run on every instantiation. Unlike the other integrations in this diff, it does not use the new `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` helper, so when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` + `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are configured (the new “sync mode”), Salesforce will still attempt to contact Salesforce directly instead of the sync endpoint; if the stored credential lacks a real `refresh_token` (a scenario the new sync-mode helpers are explicitly designed to support by tolerating responses without `refresh_token`), this refresh path will fail.
